Name: Stripe Standard API Token
Exploit:
Use the command below to verify that the Stripe Standard Live API Token is valid.
  $ curl https://api.stripe.com/v1/charges -u TOKEN_HERE:

Keep the colon at the end of the token to prevent cURL from requesting a password.

The live key can be used to extract/retrieve a lot of info ranging from the charges
to the complete product list.

Keep in mind that you will never be able to get the full credit card information since
Stripe only gives you the last 4 digits.

Name: Google API Key
Exploit:
Use the command below to verify that the API key is valid (or run pywhat with --verify):
  $ curl "https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/i18nLanguages?part=snippet&key=API_KEY_HERE"

If Google answers "API key not valid" (API_KEY_INVALID), the key is invalid. A list of languages, or an
error such as SERVICE_DISABLED or API_KEY_SERVICE_BLOCKED (the key cannot use this API), means it is valid.

There is a chance this is a Google Maps API key. Use the command below to check if it can use the paid
Geocoding API, or use 'gmapsapiscanner'[1] or 'gap'[2] to check which Google Maps services it is valid for
and generate a PoC that you can show in your report:
  $ curl "https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=40,30&key=API_KEY_HERE"

To get a better understanding of the severity of an exposed Google Maps API key, read "Unauthorized
Google Maps API Key Usage Cases, and Why You Need to Care"[3] written by Ozgur Alp (@ozguralp).

References:
 [1] https://github.com/ozguralp/gmapsapiscanner
 [2] https://github.com/joanbono/gap
 [3] https://ozguralp.medium.com/unauthorized-google-maps-api-key-usage-cases-and-why-you-need-to-care-1ccb28bf21e

API Documentation: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/get-api-key
